metadata.comment: One row of the programme. `copy` and `audience` arrive folded into the row's own data by Logic/Ordered timeline, which is how a For Each reaches a repeated component at all — and wiring `copy` through to the kit node is what TASK-L163 closes: until then TimelineRow was one of the three kit nodes handed no copy object, so it rendered its built-in English whatever the language or the audience was.

Rendered by the FIRST row of each ahead group, which is how one repeater over one ordered list draws two headed groups without the page re-deciding an order the model owns. `mounted`, never `visible`: `visible: false` is visibility:hidden in this runtime and would leave an empty eyebrow's worth of space on the other nineteen rows (measured on L157 — a 316px hole under each folded row, and a 7327px page that became 3806px). It stays OUTSIDE the kit node because a band heading is not part of a row's card.

The kit draws the row; the graph decided what it is and where it goes. The fold, the six glyphs, the two-voice wash and the one markdown path are rendering facts the catalogue cannot express — 180 node types, no SVG, no <details> (measured 2026-09-20). A kind with no glyph or card rule throws by name rather than drawing nothing (L126).

A COACH asked to see this entry in the activity log (TASK-L165). The For Each that places this row bubbles it up as itemOutputSignal-showInLog with the entry's id in itemActionItemId — the Lesson/Step chip pattern. It never fires on the learner's page, and nothing there listens for it. ALSO openLesson (TASK-L181): the learner pressed Review / Continue / Start on a lesson, or “Open the lesson this came from” on a piece of work. The same bubbling, with the entry's id in itemActionItemId; the page resolves the concept. It never fires on a coach's page.

TASK-L186. `mounted`, never `visible` (sprint 45: visibility keeps the space). Nothing under it exists until a learner presses Ask or a coach presses Reply, so forty rows carry forty closed doors and no panels.
A kit node that FETCHES NOTHING. The five Functions to the right decide every port it shows; it hands back Send requested + Body and Close requested.
